speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. You mentioned a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities, along with low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; to help me narrow this down, how many days have these symptoms been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: That timeline of a viral prodrome followed by a rash sparing the mouth is very specific. Could you describe the color and texture of the rash on her face, and has she noticed any joint pain or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of a facial rash sparing the perioral area following a viral prodrome is highly suggestive of Measles, but we must confirm this. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count with differential and Serology for Measles IgM/IgG. REQUEST IMAGES: Full_body_skin_examination_photo.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS (Note: Based on the provided data, the Complete Blood Count shows platelets slightly elevated, but the requested Measles Serology and specific image descriptions are not included in the available dataset. The skin examination notes a lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities with a facial rash sparing the perioral area, which is clinically inconsistent with the typical maculopapular rash of measles that involves the perioral area and follows a viral prodrome more characteristically associated with Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease).)

text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.
